behavioral_notes.observation: Notifications are not written eagerly: _sendone buffers {channel,message} rows into cr.precommit and the target channel into cr.postcommit. A precommit hook bulk-creates the bus.bus rows, then a postcommit hook issues SQL `SELECT pg_notify('imbus', payload)` on a dedicated 'postgres' connection. NOTIFY must fire after commit so the row is fetchable; payloads >8000 bytes are recursively split. None of this transaction-hook / pg_notify wiring is visible in metadata.

A lazily-started daemon thread runs `LISTEN imbus` on the postgres connection and uses a selector to wake on NOTIFY. On each notification it parses the channel list, looks up every websocket subscribed to those channels in the in-memory _channels_to_ws map, and calls websocket.trigger_notification_dispatching() to relay. This is the core publish/subscribe broadcast engine.

behavioral_notes.element: bus.bus._poll vs websocket dispatch (longpolling + websocket transport)
behavioral_notes.observation: Two transports coexist. _poll returns buffered notifications: on first poll (last=0) it returns rows newer than TIMEOUT(50s); otherwise rows with id>last for the subscribed channels (with ignore_ids dedup). Over websockets, Websocket._dispatch_bus_notifications acquires a cursor, calls _poll, tracks a per-socket _notif_history to avoid re-sending, and trusts the server-side last id after first subscribe rather than the client's.

Channel subscriptions are server-controlled: the client list is augmented with 'broadcast', the user's group records and (if logged in) their partner record, so a client cannot subscribe to arbitrary records. The websocket layer maintains PING/PONG heartbeat frames (HEARTBEAT_OP) with per-opcode expiration timers to detect dead connections; presence/im_status itself is computed in the JS presence service and downstream mail module, not in a bus_presence.py (which does not exist in this module).

The secure, recommended send path. _bus_send walks _bus_channel() up to a stable 'main channel' record, ensures it is a single record, optionally appends a subchannel, and delegates to bus.bus._sendone. Mixed into res.partner, res.users, res.groups, res.users.settings and ir.attachment so those records become addressable bus channels.

bus_service is the backend webclient client: it boots a SharedWorker (worker_service), sends BUS:INITIALIZE_CONNECTION/START/ADD_CHANNEL/SEND control messages, receives notification batches from the worker, tracks lastNotificationId (shared across tabs via multi_tab), and re-emits each notification by type on an EventBus that other services subscribe() to. Includes reconnection backoff and an outdated-page watcher. Not visible in Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: bus (IM Bus real-time messaging infrastructure component)
logical_data_erm: bus.bus (channel, message) -- no FK relations, channels encode (db, model, id) tuples
bus.listener.mixin -> mixed into res.partner / res.users / res.groups / res.users.settings / ir.attachment
information_flows: side-effect: any model._bus_send -> bus.bus._sendone -> bus_bus row (precommit) -> pg_notify 'imbus' (postcommit)
consumed-by: mail/discuss, web (longpolling/websocket-driven UI updates) subscribe via this bus

value_streams: Event-to-Client: model change -> _bus_send -> bus.bus row -> pg_notify -> dispatcher -> websocket -> browser update
policies: 1 access rule on bus.bus (low-level table, sudo-managed)
Channel authorization: ir.websocket._build_bus_channel_list restricts a client to broadcast + its own groups + its own partner
Autovacuum GC: bus.bus._gc_messages purges rows older than bus.gc_retention_seconds (default 24h) via direct SQL
stakeholders: Downstream modules (mail/discuss, web) that broadcast and consume
metrics: bus.monitoring_service / bus.logs_service (frontend connection health and notification logs)

classification.rationale: bus is technical real-time infrastructure (Hidden, auto_install, depends only base+web) with no business documents of its own. It is a Stabell & Fjeldstad value-shop/value-network ENABLER rather than a value activity: a small but foundational publish/subscribe layer (PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY -> websocket fan-out) that powers the collaboration and value-network features (Discuss chat, live presence, real-time UI updates) of modules layered above it. It produces no primary-chain output, so it is classified support / APQC 8.0 Manage Information Technology (deliver IT services / infrastructure).

standard_capabilities: server-controlled channel authorization (broadcast + groups + own partner)
multi-tab coordination via SharedWorker and bus_service
automatic GC of stale notifications (24h retention)
typical_fits: real-time chat/notifications out of the box once mail/discuss is installed
custom records made live by inheriting bus.listener.mixin and calling _bus_send
horizontal scaling behind a websocket-aware reverse proxy (gevent/worker)
common_gaps: new server-pushed event types require an override of _build_bus_channel_list and a JS subscribe() handler (custom dev)
very high notification volume may need ODOO_NOTIFY_PAYLOAD_MAX_LENGTH tuning or an external NOTIFY function (ODOO_NOTIFY_FUNCTION)
deployments behind proxies that do not support websocket upgrades fall back to longpolling and need configuration
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['bus.bus'].search_count([]) ; env['bus.bus'].search([], order='id desc', limit=3).read(['channel','message'])

open_questions: Exact interplay between the longpolling _poll buffer (50s window) and per-socket _notif_history dedup under reconnect storms.
How presence/im_status is computed end-to-end (lives in the JS presence service and the mail module, not in bus itself).
Operational scaling limits of the single ImDispatch thread and the postgres LISTEN connection under many concurrent websockets.
